title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Manuscript p. 748, §30, 'Enveloppes schématiques d'un T-L-groupe profini: a) Les enveloppes admissibles'. This is the continuation of 'La Longue Marche' (1981). The setting is fixed first. M is a profinite 'T-L-group', i.e. a profinite group with extra 'loop' (lacets) structure: distinguished conjugacy classes of inertia/loop elements, as for π_1 of a curve or of moduli spaces M_{g,n}. It carries a structural character χ_M : M → Ẑ^* (the cyclotomic character) with open image. Inside M sits a 'subgroup of definition' π, the geometric part, itself a profinite loop group. π_0 ⊂ π is a 'discretification': an abstract discrete loop group (e.g. a surface group with its boundary loops) whose profinite completion is π. The model is M = π_1(X_{Q-bar} → X_Q) style extensions 1 → π → M → (open in) Gal(Q-bar/Q), with χ_M the cyclotomic character, π = π_1^geom and π_0 = π_1^top.

The coefficients are then introduced. G_Q is an affine group scheme of finite type over Q. A_Q = Ẑ ⊗_Z Q ⊂ ∏_ℓ Q_ℓ is the ring of FINITE adeles. G(A_Q) ⊂ ∏_ℓ G(Q_ℓ) is described on the next page, for a Z-model G, as the restricted product: x_ℓ ∈ G(Z_ℓ) for almost all ℓ. Also from the next page: a character χ_G : G_Q → G_{m,Q} is fixed. The objects of study are homomorphisms u : M → G(A_Q) subject to admissibility conditions. Condition 1 is continuity: each component M → G(Q_ℓ) is continuous, and for ℓ outside a finite set S the map factors through G(Z_ℓ), independently of the Z-model. Presumably further conditions include compatibility χ_G∘u = χ_M (via Ẑ^* ⊂ A_Q^*). The previous page imposes quasi-unipotence of loops: on each loop subgroup L = l_i^{Ẑ} the image of some power of the generator is unipotent, in analogy with Grothendieck's ℓ-adic monodromy theorem.

The aim is to define 'admissible' adelic (i.e. simultaneously all-ℓ, almost-everywhere integral) representations of an arithmetic fundamental group into algebraic groups over Q, with a weight/cyclotomic character and quasi-unipotent local monodromy. Their Zariski closures, the 'schematic envelopes', are to give a pro-algebraic hull of M over Q: a 'motivic' Galois-Teichmüller group realized adelically.
errors: π_0 is called a 'sous-groupe discret' of π. In the profinite topology an infinite subgroup is never discrete. What is meant is an abstract (discrete) group, dense in π, with π equal to its profinite completion. This is a terminological slip, not a mathematical one.
A_Q = Ẑ⊗Q denotes the finite adeles only; there is no archimedean component. This is consistent with the ℓ-adic purpose but is non-standard notation.
Previous page, (22): 'l_i^n soit unipotent' should read 'u(l_i)^n soit unipotent'. This is a slip in the manuscript (or the transcription).
Next page, (28): G(Ẑ_ℓ) should be G(Z_ℓ).

ideas.what: Profinite group M with a cyclotomic 'structural character' M → Ẑ^*, a geometric normal subgroup π which is a profinite loop group, and a discrete model π_0 with π = (π_0)^
ideas.modern_name: Arithmetic fundamental group extension 1→π_1^geom→π_1^arith→G_Q with cyclotomic character; profinite completion of surface/braid groups with inertia classes
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (SGA1); Ihara, Deligne, Drinfeld in the Galois–Teichmüller context
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), La Longue Marche (1981, circulated) for loop groups / Teichmüller groups

ideas.what: Adelic points G(A_Q^f) of an affine Q-group of finite type as a restricted product; continuity of M → G(A_Q) meaning integrality at almost all ℓ, independent of the Z-model
ideas.modern_name: Adelic representations / compatible systems of ℓ-adic representations
ideas.usually_credited_to: Serre (Abelian ℓ-adic representations, 1968); Weil for adelic groups

ideas.what: Homomorphisms M → G(A_Q) with a character χ_G : G → G_m matching the cyclotomic character, and quasi-unipotent images of loops, whose Zariski closures ('enveloppes schématiques') form a pro-algebraic hull of M over Q
ideas.modern_name: Weighted / relative (Malcev) completion of arithmetic fundamental groups; ℓ-adic monodromy groups; motivic Galois group of mixed Tate / moduli-of-curves motives
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (relative completion, 1989 'Le groupe fondamental de la droite projective moins trois points'); Hain (relative completion, 1990s); Hain–Matsumoto (weighted completion, 2003)

ideas.what: Quasi-unipotence of loop (inertia) images imposed as an axiom of admissibility
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck's ℓ-adic monodromy theorem / quasi-unipotent local monodromy
ideas.where_published: Serre–Tate 'Good reduction of abelian varieties' appendix; SGA 7 I

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up a Q-algebraic hull of an arithmetic fundamental group (Galois–Teichmüller setting). It uses adelic representations, a G → G_m character matched with the cyclotomic character, and quasi-unipotent loops. This is structurally the same data later used in Hain–Matsumoto's weighted completion and Deligne/Hain's relative completion, which are usually built ℓ-adically one prime at a time. Here the target is simultaneously adelic, with almost-everywhere integrality.
missed.quote: On s'intéresse des homomorphismes de groupes (27) M ⟶ G(A_Q) ... On se donne de plus un hom. (26) G_Q → G_{m Q}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: An adelic, 'all ℓ at once' admissibility notion for envelopes of π_1(M_{g,n}) over Q, with a Q-structure on G rather than Q_ℓ, anticipates questions of ℓ-independence of weighted completions and motivic fundamental groups. Literature credit goes to Deligne, Hain and Matsumoto in the late 1980s–2000s.

missed.claim: The notion of 'enveloppes schématiques admissibles' of a profinite T-L-group is begun here (part a). Whether a universal envelope exists, and how it compares with motivic Galois groups, is not settled on this page.
missed.quote: (30) Enveloppes schématiques d'un T-L-groupe profini : a) Les env. admissibles.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: An adelic/Q-rational version of the Galois–Teichmüller pro-algebraic hull, with admissibility conditions on loops, is a natural object. To my knowledge it is not formalized in this form.

deep.surprise_reason: On this page, the setup of Q-rational adelic 'schematic envelopes' of arithmetic loop groups, with a cyclotomic weight character and quasi-unipotent loops, is a notable unpublished anticipation of relative/weighted completion (Deligne 1989, Hain–Matsumoto 2003). Only definitions appear here, though, and the ingredients are individually standard.
transcription_corrections: Line 'dont π s'identifie à son complété profini': 'dont' seems struck out ('[-dont-]'). Also, after 'c'est donc un', 'groupe' is struck and the text reads 'un groupe à lacets discret'. The transcription agrees on both points.
The page header number is 748 (manuscript numbering); the archive page number 200 is written at the bottom left.
'(23) A_Q = Ẑ ⊗_Z Q ⊂ ∏_{ℓ∈P} Q_ℓ' and '(24) G(A_Q) ⊂ ∏_{ℓ∈P} G(Q_ℓ)' are correctly read. P is the set of primes.
The insertion 'affine de t.f.' above the line belongs after 'schéma en groupes': 'Soit G_Q un schéma en groupes affine de t.f. sur Q'.
